add_course_source: Adds one material to a course, from a public https URL (PDF, web page or plain text, 30 MB max; redirects are not followed, so the URL must be the final one) or from pasted text. Free; the file counts toward the account's storage quota. category says what the material is: past_exam (an exam from a previous year; Cortex learns the exam format from it), lecture, exercises, notes, sample_questions (official example questions published by the teacher, whose style is imitated when there are no past exams) or exam_info (exam instructions such as a syllabus or course page, e.g. "MCQ, 45 min"); when omitted, it is guessed from the file name. The material is only stored: it is ingested when the course is prepared (prepare_course). On a free account, Cortex keeps only the material's text index, not the file (Premium keeps originals in the cloud), and its indexing starts right away, at no cost.
check_answer: Grades the student's answer to an exam question the way the course's examiner would: verdict, rubric criterion by criterion, score, feedback and a correct solution. Input: the exact question and the student's answer. Costs credits and counts toward the daily assistance quota. The first call spends nothing: it returns the exact cost and a confirmation_token. Calling again with the same arguments plus that confirmation_token runs the tool and spends the quoted credits; the token is single-use and expires. Costs per kind of generation are listed by get_account_status. When the account is not charged, the first call runs directly.
create_course: Creates a new course in the student's Cortex account, like "New course" in the app. Free. Fields: name, optional exam code (e.g. "COMP 201"), university, course language, exam date and, optionally, exam_format (type, number of questions, duration), used when the course has no past exams: Cortex never invents a format. A second course with the same exam code is refused. The course starts empty: materials are added with add_course_source and the course is built by prepare_course.
generate_drill: Generates ONE exam-style practice question on a concept, in the style of the course's real exams, with five progressive hints and a worked solution. Without a concept, it targets the student's most serious weak point. Takes up to a few minutes. Costs credits and counts toward the daily assistance quota. The first call spends nothing: it returns the exact cost and a confirmation_token. Calling again with the same arguments plus that confirmation_token runs the tool and spends the quoted credits; the token is single-use and expires. Costs per kind of generation are listed by get_account_status. When the account is not charged, the first call runs directly.
generate_mock_exam: Generates a full mock exam in the course's real exam format: multiple choice, exercises, mixed, composite questions (scenario + sub-questions), essay or oral. The format comes from the course's past exams, else from the format declared with set_exam_format, else from official sample questions or exam instructions found in its materials; when none of these says what the exam looks like, the call fails with format_required and spends nothing. format sets the type for THIS exam only (mcq = multiple-choice questions only) and takes precedence over the course's format, which is only the default. chapter (from the course plan, e.g. "3") or focus adds an emphasis on a THEME, never a format ("20 MCQ" in focus does not make a multiple-choice exam): 1-2 questions target it, the rest keeps the exam's balance. Costs credits and counts toward the daily generation quota. The first call spends nothing: it returns the exact cost and a confirmation_token. Calling again with the same arguments plus that confirmation_token runs the tool and spends the quoted credits; the token is single-use and expires. Costs per kind of generation are listed by get_account_status. When the account is not charged, the first call runs directly. After confirmation, the generation runs in the background for 10-35 minutes (longer for a large exam); its progress is read with get_job_status.
get_account_status: Returns the student's credit balance, the cost of each kind of generation (written or multiple-choice mock exam, exercise, course preparation, format detection, drill, answer check), and today's usage against the daily limits (mock exams count as generations; drills and answer checks count as assistance). usage_limits gives every limit that can stop a generation (credits, daily quotas, daily compute, monthly capacity, storage) with its reset time, and how many of each kind the student can still launch: the same numbers the app shows and the paid tools enforce. Read-only and free.
get_job_status: Returns the status, progress and current step of a long-running job started by generate_mock_exam (typically 10-35 minutes, longer for a large exam) or prepare_course. When a mock exam (written or multiple-choice) is done, it also returns its questions, the solutions when include_solutions is true, and a link to the exam in Cortex. Without job_id, it returns the generation currently running and the latest ones. Read-only and free.
get_results: Returns the student's results for a course: the mock exams Cortex generated (date, status, number of questions, verification summary, links), practice scores per topic (last score, mastery, attempts, next review) and graded feedback. Read-only and free.
get_study_plan: Returns where the student stands in a course's programme: exam countdown, coverage and mastery weighted by how often each topic appears in past exams, topics due for review, the course chapters (usable as chapter in generate_mock_exam) and a prioritised list of what to work on next. Read-only and free.
get_weak_points: Returns the student's tracked weak points for a course, most serious first (topic, theme, severity, the note explaining the gap), grouped by theme, plus the concepts due for spaced-repetition review. Read-only and free.
list_courses: Lists the courses in the signed-in student's Cortex account: id, code, name, exam date and days left. A course's id or code identifies it in the other tools. Read-only and free.
prepare_course: Builds a course from its materials, like "Prepare" in the app: ingests every material, learns the exam format from the past exams, then builds the course plan. Running it again after adding materials updates an already prepared course. Costs credits and counts toward the daily generation quota. The first call spends nothing: it returns the exact cost and a confirmation_token. Calling again with the same arguments plus that confirmation_token runs the tool and spends the quoted credits; the token is single-use and expires. Costs per kind of generation are listed by get_account_status. When the account is not charged, the first call runs directly. After confirmation, it runs in the background for several minutes; its progress is read with get_job_status.
report_question: Reports one question of a mock exam Cortex generated, with a reason: wrong_answer, off_course (not in the syllabus, or a definition that differs from the course), duplicate or ambiguous, and an optional comment. The question is identified by exam_id and its number as shown by get_job_status (multiple-choice questions first, then open ones); one call reports one question. Free: the question leaves the student's revisions and is recorded for human review, without any paid model call; a refund can follow once the error is confirmed.
search_course_materials: Full-text search in the documents the student uploaded for a course (slides, past exams, exercise sets, notes). Accent- and typo-tolerant; all words must match. Returns excerpts of about 300 characters with their source; material marked as out of the syllabus (hors programme) comes after the course material. Read-only and free.
set_exam_format: Declares (or clears) the real exam format of a course: type (qcm, exercises, mixed, essay, oral), number of questions, duration, language, documents allowed, and for multiple-choice exams whether each question has a single correct answer or several (answer_mode). Free. Past exams of the course, when present and analysed, still take precedence; otherwise mock exams follow this format (e.g. "a 20-question MCQ midterm, 45 min"). clear=true removes the declaration.
